added_failures_note: Derived with reckon.crew.review.added_failures_from_gate_logs over the reviewed run's own gate logs logs/baseline-suite.txt and logs/after-suite.txt, each read against its own recorded '# cwd resolved:' directory. Both logs are pytest format; the baseline arm reports no FAILED id with '58 passed' and EXIT=0, the after arm reports no FAILED id with '60 passed' and EXIT=0, so the added-failure set is empty and the count is a measured zero. Instrument check before reporting the absence: the same readers return FAILED tests/test_a_released_review_is_composed_again.py::test_a_released_composed_review_is_composed_again from logs/negative-control-mutated.txt and logs/base-revision-new-test.txt, so an empty column here is the logs' measured result rather than a blind reader.

assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Reinstating the base behaviour (releasing without writing back to the reviewed run) leaves the dispatch record at status 'dispatched' at that head, _failed_review_backend withholds the lane at reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:1843, and the recompose refuses with 'no eligible lane'; logs/base-revision-new-test.txt records exactly that red at 2424ab7511.

Dropping the _record_review_dispatch call at reckon/crew/admission/launching.py:658 leaves the record's status at 'dispatched' and the assertion reddens; logs/negative-control-mutated.txt shows the reddening with that write mutated out.
Stamping the record for a different run id, or dropping review_run_id from the reason, reddens; the expected value is the minted review run id, not a value the helper passed in.
Recording a different head on the recomposed attempt, or recomposing for a run resumed past the released head, reddens; head is captured at :190 from the delivered run before the release.
Returning the released id, or composing nothing at all, reddens; the composed id must be a new id whose pointer exists.

No condition in this file makes it fail: the reviewed run's pointer is removed by promotion.discard before the release, so the helper returns on the missing pointer whether or not the promotion.discard_recorded guard at launching.py:642 exists.

findings.text: The discarded-run case's no-write assertion does not pin the guard it was added beside: after promotion.discard the reviewed run's pointer is already gone (asserted at :234), so deleting the promotion.discard_recorded guard at reckon/crew/admission/launching.py:642 leaves the helper returning at :646 on the CrewError that runs.read_pointer raises for the missing pointer, no record reappears, and :242 stays green. The branch that must not stamp a discarded run is unexercised.

The promoted-run guard has no test at all: deleting the runs._promoted_record_project check here leaves both cases in tests/test_a_released_review_is_composed_again.py green, so nothing fails if a released composed review stamps the dispatch record of a run the fleet has already promoted, which a later reader would read as the promoted run owing a review.
